steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Have you started packing your gear, Aurora?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Yeah. We've finished organizing the samples and testing materials, right?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Starting preparations today will make things much smoother if we're going back tomorrow.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Well, I've got a new proposal. We actually have some room on the schedule, and it happens to be aurora season. How about we push the return trip back a couple of days?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Of course! Pushing it back two days will put us right on schedule. I wanted to do something for my 'assistant surveyor', who helped me so much on this trip.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Just doing my job, Maggy.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I wouldn't have accepted the offer if I didn't think there was something I could help with.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: So we're good on this? We'll stay two days, then we'll head back if we still don't see the aurora.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Thanks, Maggy.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Could I ask a favor?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I want to use these two days to continue testing the new defensive shield. Can I use the camera drone to record the testing?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I have a camera module on my own shield, but it can't run autonomously.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: The shield's Originium circuits aren't fully stable either, and it's safer to have a drone record from a distance than to have a person operate the camera.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Sure. I'll show you how to set it up.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Alright. I'm gonna go further away, because it might get loud.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Be sure to holler if there's a problem!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And there I was, thinking I was giving her two days of rest. She was always running ahead when we were looking for samples.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: She may be Ursus, but she's a patient too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: And she keeps talking about the shield—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Is that wind?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Tall, dark clouds with indistinct edges...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Aurora—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Aurora!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Maggy, get into protective gear!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I've seen these clouds before. Could be an Originium hail. It—

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Get behind me! Stay behind the barriers and put on protective gear. We already have injured students!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: There's Originium in the hail! Be careful!

steps.name: Scared Student
steps.text: Lara! Your shoulder...?

steps.name: Brave Student
steps.text: I'll take over the barrier. Get back, Lara!

steps.name: Brave Student
steps.text: You've been hit by Originium hail!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Stay behind me, Maggy!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I've been through this kind of Originium hail before. The risk of infection is very high. Make sure you keep that protective suit tight around you!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Is your suit on, Maggy? Help me with mine after you're done—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I'm done!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Listen, Aurora. I've encountered this stuff before. Let's go back and use those rocks for cover. We won't last five minutes out in the open!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: But I won't be able to protect you properly on the move!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But you'll definitely get hurt in the open!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I have experience with these things. I can take care of myself. Don't—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Watch your leg! The strap on your suit is loose!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I'll protect you, Maggy. We'll go, but I'll carry you.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Curl up and stay under my shield!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I can run by myself! I'm not afraid of the hail. I'm worried that you—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Are all Ursus so strong? If you try to carry me, you'll—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Aurora!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: We're here, safe and sound.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Are you crazy?! Let me check your suit!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: One second, Maggy.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I want to get the barrier set up by the rock. I'm not sure we can keep it up by ourselves.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Alright, you talk first. I'm definitely gonna check, though. We'll need a new plan, if there's the slightest hint of a gap—do you need the drone for anything?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Absolutely no gaps between the rocks and the shield where hail might come through. It's so cramped in here, there'll be no room to dodge.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Looks like we'll need to submit another modification application when we get back.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: We need portable equipment to set up protection quickly, away from well-supplied bases, without having to rely on individual aptitude and reactions.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: We're lucky there are suitable rocks nearby... oh, and I brought the camera drone that you lent me too.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Drone? Just leave stuff like that in an emergency! Get yourself to safety first!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I kno—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: What is it, Aurora? Why did you suddenly go quiet?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Something's not right, Maggy.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Move over a little, let me look outside.
Magallan pokes her head out from behind Aurora and peeks through a crack.
The sun has been completely blocked out by the dark clouds, while Originium-filled hail blasts at the shield from all directions, surrounding it and the pair behind it.

The wind rushes at the filter of the protective mask, and the mixture of sleet makes it almost impossible to breathe. Ice shards cut through Aurora's gloves, but she continues to grab the shield tightly.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: My shield won't last long. It wasn't designed to protect against Originium events. Most of my equipment is back at the base.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: The hail shouldn't last too long. Leave the drones outside; they can help clear up some of it. I think we'll make it—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Angle the shield inwards a little bit more. Right now, it's putting to much of a burden on you, and it's hard for me to apply any force!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I have two plans, Maggy.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Plan A. You stay here with the shield, while I go back to the base and come back with proper barriers. You'll be absolutely safe here.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Plan B. I'll change the shield to the prototype that I'm still testing, but it might—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Plan B.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: If you want to charge out by yourself because I'm not Infected, I'll be coming with you, no matter what, because I'm not accepting that kind of help.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You stay here. I have an idea, even if the prototype doesn't work. We can move along the rocks and try to find a hollow space to hide in.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Don't try to carry everything on your shoulders!
Aurora reaches for the prototype shield.
She began developing its Originium circuit while she was still at Ironforge Polytechnic. She wanted to return to Kjerag with a breakthrough in defensive technology.
She went to great lengths to be able to go to the world outside, even getting into a fight with her father.

steps.name: Lara's Father
steps.text: Why do you insist on going out there, Lara?

steps.name: Lara's Father
steps.text: There are machines in the mines. You can work under Enciodes. Kjeragandr will protect Kjerag and His people!

steps.name: Lara's Father
steps.text: Why won't you work for the future with me and your brother in the mines?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I believe in Kjeragandr, but I don't want to see the names of other countries on the machines we use in the mines!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I want the name of Kjerag on them!

steps.name: Brave Student
steps.text: Aurora, get back! Your suit is broken!

steps.name: Brave Student
steps.text: Why do you insist on being in front? Because you think you can? It's a Catastrophe!

steps.name: Brave Student
steps.text: You might be infected already! Leave the barrier to me! I'm in better shape than you are!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: No, I'm staying here!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I designed the barrier, I know how to use it best!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Since I'm already hurt, I should be the one standing in front to protect the ones who aren't hurt!
The Originium in Aurora's body aches. The hail that fell upon the ice and upon Aurora now falls before her.

She recalls the letter from her parents after they learned about her infection, the igloo that she built with her friends, Enciodes's staffing proposal, trains rushing by, and the high-rises of Columbia.
Outside the shield, the hail presses on. She can smell it through her mask.
Am I afraid?

a.text: I'm afraid my life will change because of this. I'm afraid that my parents will worry about me.
But I'm most afraid that I won't be able to do what I could have—

steps.text: The shield is right behind her, the circuit on the back is still unfinished, because of her condition.
It is what she has longed to accomplish, her long-time dream, what keeps her standing up front, each and every time.
The hail is getting fiercer, and she feels Magallan's hands frantically trying to help support the barrier.
Aurora raises the prototype shield.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Aurora?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You can't run so much Arts at the same time. It'll overload you!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: It won't, Maggy. I want to try it.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I developed this shield to protect my home and the people around me.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: This is what it's made for. And this is the time to give my all.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I became infected with Oripathy because I couldn't do enough. I won't let it happen again.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I don't want to disappoint you, disappoint anybody else, or disappoint myself!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: This is my choice, and I'll see it through.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: How could I talk about protecting all of Kjerag, if I can't even protect you, here and now?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: You've got the experience, Maggy! Tell me what to do to protect both of us once it's activated!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Activating drone offensive module. Move over a little, Aurora.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Listen for my cue once it's activated, and I'll blast the hail away!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: How are you feeling, Aurora?

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: We're at the supply station that we left from, located at where the barrens meet the Icefields.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You passed out right after the hail ended. The prototype shield was damaged, but I knew you wouldn't throw it away, so I brought it here after cleaning it up.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: ...Are you hurt, Maggy? No infections or anything?!

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: No infections, just a couple of flesh wounds.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Whew... I thought I had to—

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You thought you had to shield me with your torso? That's what your body language said. Protecting yourself is always the priority on the Icefields.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You need to keep yourself safe in order to keep others safe.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Maggy, I...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: You want to see your shield, right? Here, all cleaned up and wrapped up.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Maggy, I... Catastrophes are avoidable, right?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Not saying that we can stop them from happening, but if we had operated according to plan, we would have been back at base, going through the supplies in safety, while watching the hail fall outside...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Aurora.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I knew you'd think that way. Irregular events are a regularity when you do research this far north.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I've encountered blizzards that kept me in an ice hole for five full days. I've encountered avalanches that buried all my drones. And don't get me started on invisible cracks in glaciers...

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: The north doesn't change for anybody. We get what we want from it on our own, and pay the appropriate price.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: A few months of solitude, or some kind of injury... this is what we deal with all the time.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: The north doesn't cause a Catastrophe just because you decided to delay a few days. It does what it wants, and we just happened to run into it. Don't blame yourself.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Well, I wanted to let you see the aurora with your own eyes...
Magallan takes out a heavily-damaged drone.
Its camera module is connected to a data cable, and the screen is showing an intermittent video recording.
The little corner of sky visible from the edge of the shield is obscured by clouds and hail. Then, a single ray of light shines through.
Like a veil of silk, it slowly begins to cover the clouds.
It's at that time that Aurora lowers her head, and the shield's Originium circuit glows a bright blue, indicating overload.
Aurora presses at the barrier, forming an impregnable line of defense, as Originium and hail bounce off the shield.
The sky shines brightly with a myriad of colors.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I saw this recording when I was taking stock of the remaining supplies. The drone's camera kept running, showing that we actually encountered the aurora that you wanted to see.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: But it was me who proposed that we stay two more days, Aurora.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: I know the north better than you do, and I know better what we're dealing with here.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: That's why I wanted to wait until you saw the aurora with your own eyes.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Maggy!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Maggy—

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: My goal has always been to achieve what I wanted under my own strength and hard work.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: What I care about is that I managed to protect ourselves from the hail, and that you haven't been infected! And I completed the project I've been working on for so long!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Now I can tell my parents and siblings that I never stopped trying, even with my illness. I achieved a lot, and I'm gradually realizing my dream!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: And I can tell myself that I made the right choice. It's not about seeing the aurora; it's about successfully accomplishing these things.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: That's why this video is even more precious to me than seeing the aurora with my own eyes!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Look here, Maggy.
Aurora excitedly adjusts the playback bar until it stops on a particular frame:
Magallan is stretching out her arms, supporting Aurora's body, while a drone flies above the shield under her command.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Look! The drone didn't just record me supporting the defenses; it caught you on camera too!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: We're in this shot together, under the aurora!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I love this recording sooooo much! This was a great mission!

a.text:
Dear Lara,
The data you sent back has been received. The mines are planning to employ the new technology in mining equipment.

spans.text:
Dear Lara,
The data you sent back has been received. The mines are planning to employ the new technology in mining equipment.

a.text: Dad and I received the photo as well. I'm putting it up with the Kjeragandr, so I can see you working hard every day.

spans.text: Dad and I received the photo as well. I'm putting it up with the Kjeragandr
, so I can see you working hard every day.

a.text: Dad made some heat-to-eat cheese fondue packs for you. They'll last a long time.

spans.text: Dad made some heat-to-eat cheese fondue packs for you. They'll last a long time.

a.text: We're always worried about you, but we support you and we're proud of you. Your life is your own. We'll be here, waiting for your good news.

spans.text: We're always worried about you, but we support you and we're proud of you. Your life is your own. We'll be here, waiting for your good news.

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: Maggy! Where are you?

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I've been thinking about the next expedition, and I've been working with Engineering to come up with a draft for that new equipment I wanted to make!

steps.name: Aurora
steps.text: I have a few other operators here who are interested. Let's talk things over.

steps.name: Magallan
steps.text: Coming!
